subject: Getting different (but similar) results in unmarked and presence

messages.author: fd7b4a4c5f51fc06
messages.subject: Getting different (but similar) results in unmarked and presence
parts:
Hi everyone,

I apologize if I'm doing something stupid, but I am unable to get the same results when running my simplest dynamic occupancy models in unmarked and Presence. I've run a series of models in Presence, and am now trying to duplicate it in unmarked to make sure I actually understand what I'm doing. I am using the same input file for both (8 years of coverboard surveys for blue-spotted salamanders at 234 sites, not all sites checked each year, rotating panel design). My code works as far as I can tell, and I'm able to get very similar results for each model I run. I present example code for just the basic m0 model:



library(tidyverse)
library(beepr)
options(digits=4)
setwd("C:/Users/John/Dropbox/Grad School/PhD/NIU/Lake County/RAMP/Ambystoma/R scripts/Laterale Files/Laterale Project/Occupancy")
laterale <- read_csv("C:/Users/John/Dropbox/Grad School/PhD/NIU/Lake County/RAMP/Ambystoma/R scripts/Laterale Files/Laterale Project/Occupancy/laterale_inp_ms.csv",na = "-")
laterale$WMP <- as.factor(laterale$WMP)
glimpse(detections <- laterale[,2:33])
glimpse(sitecovs <- laterale[,34:39])
laterale_UMF <- unmarkedMultFrame(
    y = detections,
    siteCovs = sitecovs,
    numPrimary = 8)
summary(laterale_UMF) # This does not show yearly site covariates.
m0 <- colext(psiformula=~1, #first year occupancy
             gammaformula=~1, #colonization
             epsilonformula=~1, #extinction
             pformula=~1, #detection
             data = laterale_UMF)
coef(m0)
plogis(coef(m0)) #inverse logit function
backTransform(m0, type="det") #computes SE using delta method
backTransform(m0, type="psi")
backTransform(m0, type="col")
backTransform(m0, type="ext")
models <- fitList('m0 psi(.)gam(.)eps(.)p(.)' = m0)
ms <- modSel(models)
ms
beep(3)
library(unmarked)


This results in:

                                        nPars     AIC       delta    AICwt   cumltvWt
m0 psi(.)gam(.)eps(.)p(.)               4         1035.95    0.00    1.00     1.00

and

psi(Int) col(Int) ext(Int)   p(Int)
-1.4881  -3.0195  -3.7359   0.2008

However, when I use the same input data in presence, and run the same model (Run > Analysis:multi-season > simple multi-season) and use all the default values, I get a different AIC values:

"Model"                           AIC         deltaAIC  AIC wgt  Model Likelihood no.Par.   -2*LogLike
"psi,gamma(),eps(),p()"           1421.06     0.00      1.0000   1.0000           4         1413.06

and

Untransformed Estimates of coefficients for covariates (Beta's)
======================================================================
             estimate std.error
A1 psi1   : -1.408162 0.212786
B1 gam(1) : -2.909684 0.184862
C1 eps(1) : -3.093341 0.459359
D1 P[1-1] : -0.016745 0.098899


As you can see, these are small differences, but I'd like to know if I am doing something wrong.

Also, the output of summary(laterale_UMF) results in: 

234 sites
Maximum number of observations per site: 32
Mean number of observations per site: 9.28
Number of primary survey periods: 8
Number of secondary survey periods: 4
Sites with at least one detection: 0

Is there a reason it says there are no sites with at least one detection? Could this be where things are calculated differently?

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Getting different (but similar) results in unmarked and presence
parts:
for what it's worth here's the line of code that prints out the "Sites with at least one detection' summary:

cat("Sites with at least one detection:",
        sum(apply(getY(object), 1, function(x) any(x > 0, na.rm=TRUE))),
        "\n\n")

Its possible that this is not doing something wrong but it should be easy to check by applying to your data object directly. In any case this is independent of the likelihood calculations.

I don't have any ideas on the difference between unmarked and PRESENCE.  For this type of problem I would recommend a small simulation study using data similar to your data (same missing value structure, etc..). I'll put it on my "to do list" which may take some time.

regards
andy
